findings.text: The first sentence tells a newcomer what Athena is in plain words. They can say what it is right away.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: The page says why it exists: it is a sample of Athena's output, and every statement can be traced to source lines. The claim links to pinned GitHub lines back this up, so the reader can see why it matters.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The next step appears in the header, so the reader knows what to do before reaching the long detail. But the Next steps section only gives repository links. There is no install command and no example request, so 'install Athena' still means going somewhere else.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself."

findings.text: At Athena's own URL, almost all of the page covers firstmate internals: exit codes, places-held, and 44 claims. Two sentences cover Athena. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets a long demo and very little about the tool.
findings.source: Heading "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the sections States, Counters, Transitions, Why it is built this way, Claims and sources

findings.text: The page names cost tracking and a separate checking model as Athena features, but shows neither for this study. There is no cost, no model names and no record of a check. The traceability claim is shown; these two are not.
findings.source: "records what each step cost" and "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it"

findings.text: Firstmate is named in the title and the header but not explained until after the 'Words used first' list. That list defines captain, yolo, green and red before the reader knows what firstmate is.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate" (header) before "What firstmate is" (under Start here)

findings.text: This is the third paragraph of the header, and it gives a repository detail a newcomer does not need yet. It delays the actual content.
findings.source: "Its study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The finding ids jump from f1 to f3 with no f2, which makes a careful reader wonder what was left out. The section is otherwise honest that nothing was run: "no run confirmed that a script behaves as its header says."
findings.source: Heading "Limits of this study": items f1, f3, f4

findings.text: The page says plainly where its sources are silent, here and in the no-bound statements about relaunches and retries. That builds trust in the claim-tracing approach.
findings.source: "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."
